title: Extended ideal powers annihilate quotient-sheaf sections
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal, $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec} A$. Let $J=I\mathcal O_X$ be the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $n\in\mathbb N$ put $Q=F/J^nF$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For every $a\in I^n$, open $U\subseteq X$, and $t\in Q(U)$, the restriction to $U$ of the global function $f^*(a)$ acts by zero on $t$. No properness, coherence, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 02OC, annihilation of the quotient by I^n; Modules Tags 01AG and 01CB for the stalk argument

proof.text: For n = 0, the ideal power inclusion is the identity of the unit module. Its multiplication map is the left unitor, hence epic. Its image inclusion is epic and its cokernel is zero. Evaluation gives a subsingleton section module.

At x use ideal_module_product_stalk to obtain the unit-stalk comparison e, the stalk ideal K, and the positive-power quotient equivalence. For b in I, the Mathlib pullback-ideal adjunction L <= (L.comap f).map f and ideal_ker_le show that f*(b) is killed by J.subschemeι. The sectionwise kernel range of J.toModulesι gives a global ideal section lifting f*(b). Take its germ and apply e to conclude that g(b) belongs to K.

Ideal.map_pow and monotonicity of powers imply g(a) belongs to K^(n+1). Lift the germ of t through the linear quotient equivalence and choose a quotient representative y. The product g(a) smul y belongs to K^(n+1) smul top, so its quotient class is zero. Linearity transports this to zero in the quotient stalk.
Use germ_smul and germ_res_apply to identify this zero stalk element with the germ of the claimed scalar multiple. Mathlib Presheaf.section_ext proves the section equality.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02OC, with Modules Tags 01AG and 01CB; F3 second reading realizes the stalk argument using Mathlib ideal pullback adjunction and the existing quotient-stalk equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem formalModuleQuotient_scalar_zero {A : Type v} [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) {X : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A))
    (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hJ : J = (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom)).comap f)
    (F : X.Modules) (n : ℕ) (a : A) (ha : a ∈ I ^ n)
    (U : X.Opens) (t : (formalModuleQuotient J n F).val.obj (op U)) :
    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top (a := U))).op).hom
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom a) • t = 0
